<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->
<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->

<!-- In addition to that please answer these questions: -->

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

fixes https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/18819

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

Yes, but only when:
- `output.target` doesn't support dynamic import
- you don't have `browserslist` and your browsers don't support dynamic import
- you don't specify `chunkFormat` directly


Before - `chunkFormat: "array-push"` when `experiments.outputModule: true` 
Now - `chunkFormat: "module"` when `experiments.outputModule: true`

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

No
pr_comments:
<!-- identifier: admin-actions -->

*For maintainers only:*

* [ ] <!-- document --> This needs to be documented (issue in webpack/webpack.js.org will be filed when merged)
* [ ] <!-- webpack-4-backport --> This needs to be backported to webpack 4 (issue will be created when merged)

To be honest, I think it's more intuitive, when the user specifies `experiments.outputModule` and does not specify any additional options (like `browserslist`, extra target `es2020` and etc), by default it is correct to generate `module` chunk format instead `array-push`

It's not only about `chunkFormat` and `environment.dynamicImport`,  I also found that esm library module is hard to understand and configure in  webpack, cause you need to configure multi option together to make it work like https://github.com/rspack-contrib/rspack-examples/blob/main/rspack/library-esm/rspack.config.mjs. 
so I think a better idea is to provide preset option provide out of box default configuration for all other option,and other option is used to fine tune for specific usage case.
It seems `experiments.outputModule` is good candidate for preset option
* `experiments.outputModule:true`: means set default option of `environment.dynamicImport=true` `output.module=true` & `output.library = "modern-module"` & `chunkFormat: "module"` together, there can also be other preset option like `esnext` or `nodenext` for other default option, and user still can setup  `output.library=module` to override default option setup by `outputModule:true`

IMO `experiments.outputModule` is just a switcher, it does nothing except let user can set `output.module` to `true`, and `output.module` is the real option that implies other options need to be esm default.
In this way user can have minimal migration cost once `experiments.outputModule` become stable, user only needs to remove it and other options stay as is.

The `output.module` is marked as an experimental feature in the documentation, so it may potentially break at some time. Users adopting `output.module` likely want to utilize more ESM features, so this change should not be a major issue. The `experiments.outputModule` flag is simply meant to indicate that features like `output.module` are not yet stable.

@hardfist @ahabhgk @fi3ework 

The main problem - we've always had - https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/main/lib/config/defaults.js#L924 and it is based on - options.experiments.outputModule...

So we need decide, what we will change to avoid misleading:

> experiments.outputModule:true: means set default option of environment.dynamicImport=true output.module=true & output.library = "modern-module" & chunkFormat: "module" together, there can also be other preset option like esnext or nodenext for other default option, and user still can setup output.library=module to override default option setup by outputModule:true

or

> IMO experiments.outputModule is just a switcher, it does nothing except let user can set output.module to true, and output.module is the real option that implies other options need to be esm default.
In this way user can have minimal migration cost once experiments.outputModule become stable, user only needs to remove it and other options stay as is.

Yeah, it was a small breaking change, but the behavior will be more predictable

Honestly, in the future I think we shouldn't have `experiments.outputModule` and `output.module` options at all (when it will be stabilized).

We will use `chunkFormat: "module"` by default (if it is not specified) when the user environment (i.e. browserslist or target) supports `import`'s. I think it's better DX, if he wants to use another - chunk format - you can set your target or change `chunkFormat` manually. It seems to me to form settings/options from the specified environment is good DX, less options.

That's why I raised this question, maybe we can now standardize this behavior and make it more intuitive.

TLDR:

> I think we should keep current design, and let all esm output related default option be controlled by output.module other than environment




I think there's a more general question here?
what experiments flags means in webpack?, a turn on switcher or a  preset ? we may need a coherent design here.
the current design is
experiments.css & experiments.outputModule plays like both **switcher** and **preset** now

* as a switcher you need to turn on experiments.outputModule and experiments.css) so you can use other related option, otherwise it will throw error 
* as a preset when you turn on experiments.css it means the default type for `.css` is `css` and default output.module and output.chunkFormat is true when turn on experiments.outputModule

I agree with @ahabhgk's idea, outputModule should be the preset option, but use experiments.outputModule to control output.module default value even not ideal but still sounds good to me.

> IMO experiments.outputModule is just a switcher, it does nothing except let user can set output.module to true, and output.module is the real option that implies other options need to be esm default.

I'm fine with current design(experiments.outputModule controls output.module default controls output.chunkFormat default)
* before experiments.xxxFlags is stable: (experiments.xxxFlag -> experiments.xxxPresetOptions -> experients.xxx{option1,option2,option3)
* after experiments.xxxFlags is stable: (experiments.xxxPresetOptions -> experients.xxx{option1,option2,option3})

The current problem is actually
* since we don't stablize experiments.outputModule yet, experiments.outputModule  and output.module seems redundant, that can be solved when we stablize experiments.outputModule and remove experiments.outputModule
* the `output.module` doesn't control all options which should be affected by esm output(like environment)



> We will use chunkFormat: "module" by default (if it is not specified) when the user environment (i.e. browserslist or target) supports import's

I don't think use `environment` to control `chunkFormat` is a good idea here. they are separate semantic, and actually we have internal framework use custom chunkFormat while environment is very modern(think of quickjs runtime ships latest ecma feature but may not support esm at all), so `module` and `ecma syntax` support should be treated separately(that's also what typescript is doing)

another thing is that if  `environment` | `target` affect too much things(it already affect js transformer & runtime target & css transformer & minify transformer), it will be really hard to configure it

@hardfist 

> I don't think use environment to control chunkFormat is a good idea here. they are separate semantic, and actually we have internal framework use custom chunkFormat while environment is very modern(think of quickjs runtime ships latest ecma feature but may not support esm at all), so module and ecma syntax support should be treated separately(that's also what typescript is doing)

Why? If I have `browserslist` and browsers support `import`, let's use `module` chunk format (not now, after we stability experiments.outputModule). It's quite intuitive. Note - environment is being formed from `browserslist` or `target`

So what decision will we have regarding the current change? Because we can implement it differently and required to set `output.module`, so shortly what we want:

- `F(output, "module", () => Boolean(experiments.outputModule));`
- `F(output, "module", () => false);` and we required to set `output.module` if you want ESM

To be honest, both decisions are definitely breaking changes (but we are in `experiments` so it should be fine).

I prefer the first. 

I will wait until we come to a common decision so that we do not disagree in our behavior for options.

@hardfist friendly ping

Briefly, what I did here is that I now - simply use an optimistic check to see if dynamic import works to use the module format, previously it was not optimistic - https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/18822/files#diff-c0078e4713a0e7a24dbc56d6dfda3cf139376325fc65ea70a8389d4d30b27f04R1084

this change LGTM，so basically we only change to set chunk format to module when output.module is true and dynamic import works, so if output.module is false nothing changed

issue_context.title: `library.type module` and `optimization.runtimeChunk single` will nest `export` inside `__webpack_require__` callback
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the GitHub Discussions. -->
<!-- https://github.com/webpack/webpack/discussions -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**
`library.type module` and `optimization.runtimeChunk single` will nest `export` inside `__webpack_require__` callback

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**
webpack.config.js
```
module.exports = {
  entry: {
    main: {
      import: './main.js',
      library: { type: 'module' },
    },
  },
  optimization: {
    runtimeChunk: 'single',
  },
  experiments: {
    outputModule: true,
  },
  mode: 'development',
  devtool: false,
}
```

main.js
```
console.log('main');
export const main = 'MAIN';
```

output:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14d12cb0-e792-4257-8e7a-a60d16ca8672)
